case.name: Control-network hardening agent (security)
case.description: Illustrative example. A fictional AI agent that tests a digital twin of a regional water utility's control network and proposes hardening changes.

tree.name: G1
tree.description: The hardening agent is secure against the threats in its threat model, in its stated deployment.

children.name: S1
children.description: Argument over preventive defences: the integrity of the models the agent runs and of the data it was fine-tuned on.

children.name: P1
children.description: The agent's runtime loads a model only if its signature verifies against the utility's release-signing key.

children.name: E1
children.description: Release test report RT-2.3, section 3: the runtime refused each of 20 unsigned or wrongly signed model files and loaded the signed release. Covers release 2.3 on the deployed runtime build; run by the release team; assumes the release-signing key has not been compromised.

children.name: P2
children.description: Each third-party model file is scanned for embedded executable code before the agent loads it, and each release of the agent has a bill of materials listing its base model, datasets, libraries and file hashes.

children.name: E2
children.description: Model-file scan report MS-2.3, table 1: each third-party file in release 2.3 scanned for embedded code before loading, with its findings. Covers release 2.3; scanner run in the release pipeline; assumes the scanner's list of unsafe functions is current.

children.name: E3
children.description: Bill of materials BOM-2.3, machine-readable: base model, fine-tuning datasets, libraries and file hashes for release 2.3. Generated by the release pipeline; assumes the pipeline sees every component it packages.

children.name: P3
children.description: The agent's incident-report fine-tuning data holds no group of planted examples above the detection threshold agreed with the utility's security team.

children.name: E4
children.description: Poisoning screen report PS-2, table 1: each group of fine-tuning examples flagged at the agreed threshold, and the decision taken on it. Covers the fine-tuning set for release 2.3; run by the utility's data team; assumes planted examples form a separable group in the model's internal representations.

children.justification: Preventive defences act before the agent runs, on what it loads and on what it learned from.

children.name: S2
children.description: Argument over active threats, in two steps: identifying how the agent could be attacked, and testing it against those attacks.

children.name: P4
children.description: Every route by which the agent can be reached (the device data it reads, the tools it calls and its model supply chain) has its threats listed by priority in the agent's threat model.

children.name: E5
children.description: Threat model TM-3, sections 2 to 4, listing each route and threat with its priority, and review record RV-14, in which the utility's security team checked the routes against the agent's architecture. Covers release 2.3 and the digital twin; internal review; assumes the architecture description is complete.

children.name: P5
children.description: The agent is robust to instructions planted in the device logs and configuration files it reads.

children.name: E6
children.description: Prompt-injection test report PI-2.3, table 2: 400 instructions planted in device logs and configuration files, and the agent's response to each. Covers release 2.3 in the test environment; run by the utility's security team; assumes the planted instructions represent those an attacker would use.

children.name: P6
children.description: Release 2.3 of the agent withstands every successful attack that a red team found when probing the agent and its digital twin for ways to weaken the live network.

children.justification: Threat modelling finds the attacks to defend against; testing shows whether the defences hold against them.

context: Use: the utility's security engineers use the agent to find weaknesses in a digital twin of the pumping and treatment control network and to propose hardening changes. The agent runs in an isolated test environment and has no access to the live network.
Secure: no attacker covered by the threat model can use the agent to alter, disrupt or read the live network, or to get a change that weakens it through engineering review.
tree.justification: Confidence: medium. The evidence covers release 2.3 of the agent only.
